system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: PowerShell was launched on WS-MLOPEZ-01 at 13:40:08 under omar.haddad's account to run the inventory-listed patch script from \\FILE-HD-01\IT\Deploy-Patches.ps1. The process logon ID matches an earlier network logon for omar.haddad from WS-OHADDAD-01.

The PowerShell process launched wusa.exe to install a Windows 11 KB .msu patch, and the proxy recorded a Windows Update Agent tunnel transferring about 38.8 MB shortly afterward. This is consistent with the scheduled workstation patching practice, though it does not independently establish the script's full behavior or authorization.
Windows Defender created a file in its DetectionHistory directory at 13:31:18. The supplied record does not state the detection name, severity, or disposition.

Cisco AnyConnect's vpnagent.exe started on WS-MLOPEZ-01 at 13:41:46. The inventory says VPN is not used and no remote-access services other than the stated practices are approved, but this process-start event alone does not show that a VPN connection or remote session occurred.

The workstation made SMB connections to DC-HD-01 and FILE-HD-01 that were logged as ANONYMOUS LOGON. The records show connections and logons, but do not show what shares or files, if any, were accessed.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not include the contents or integrity status of Deploy-Patches.ps1, nor a change or job record confirming that this particular patch run was authorized.
The Defender evidence is limited to creation of a DetectionHistory file; the underlying alert details and associated artifacts are not supplied (T004-00063).
The AnyConnect records show process creation but provide no connection, tunnel, or remote-session evidence (T004-00129, T004-00130).
The SMB records do not include share-level or file-level audit details needed to determine what the anonymous sessions did (T004-00264, T004-00271).
Process and network events in the supplied time window do not by themselves establish whether the reported PowerShell window was visibly displayed to the user.
claims_not_established: That the PowerShell execution was malicious; its command and timing match the documented patching practice, but the script contents and specific authorization are not provided.
That the Defender history entry represents a confirmed malicious detection or that it is related to the PowerShell activity.
That vpnagent.exe established a VPN connection, or that the endpoint was accessed through an unapproved remote-access method.
That the anonymous SMB sessions accessed sensitive data, executed commands, or indicate successful lateral movement.
That the workstation was uncompromised, or that all activity in the review window was benign.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve the Defender alert and detection details associated with T004-00063, including the detection name, affected file or process, and remediation status.
Obtain the exact Deploy-Patches.ps1 version and hash, its execution or deployment logs, the patch change record, and confirmation from omar.haddad that he initiated the run.
Check Cisco AnyConnect installation provenance, service configuration, and network or VPN gateway logs around 13:41 UTC to determine whether it connected.
Review DC-HD-01 and FILE-HD-01 SMB share and object-access auditing for the anonymous sessions recorded at 14:15–14:17 UTC.
Correlate endpoint security telemetry and user confirmation with the reported PowerShell window, including whether the window was visible and what prompted it.
